```{r libraries, warning=FALSE}
library("clustGLMM")
library("colorspace")
```

## Creating example dataset

Our example dataset consists of young male people observed repeatedly in their age span of 18-40 years. Each person has its id variable `i` and `j` denotes the number of observation for that particular person. The total number of observations $n_i$ per person differs and the times of examination are uniformly spread along the age years of 18-40. 

We observe three outcomes:

* `income` the average income over last year (in artificial units),
* `ntrips` number of trips in the last year
* `satisfaction` the level of satisfaction (0=dissatisfied < 1=neither-nor < 2=satisfied)

```{r dataset}
source("generate_student_example_data.R")
set.seed(31415)
# n <- 2000
n <- 500
llist <- generate_student_example_data(n)
data <- llist$data
data$nogroup <- rep(0, dim(data)[1])
head(data[,c("i", "j", "g", "age", "income", "ntrips", "satisfaction")], 15)
summary(as.factor(table(data$i))) # summary of total observation counts
summary(data[,c("age", "income", "ntrips", "satisfaction")])
```

```{r save_dataset, eval=FALSE}
students <- data[,c("i", "j", "g", "age", "income", "ntrips", "satisfaction", "b_num", "b_poi", "b_ord")]
save(students, file="C:/Users/jvavra/OneDrive - WU Wien/Documents/PhD/clustGLMM/data/students.RData")
```

## Plotting longitudinal data

### Numerical outcome - student income vs. age
In general there seems to be an increasing trend.
```{r income, echo=TRUE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
par(mar=c(4,4,1,0.5))
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, "income", x="age", g="nogroup", legend_placement="topleft")
```

However, on closer look (having the true clustering variable `g` at disposal) there could be seen 2 to 3 groups of different evolution. One group clearly has slower income increase than the other.

Interpretation:

* group 1 (red): people who did not study at university start to earn money earlier;
* group 2+3 (green, blue): university degree helps these people to start their career with steeper increase of income. Hard-working ones (blue) have slightly higher income. 
```{r grouped_income, echo=TRUE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
par(mar=c(4,4,1,0.5))
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, "income", x="age", g="g", legend_placement="topleft")
```

### Count outcome - number of trips income vs. age
When young, people have plenty of time for going on trips. Then, as the university is studied and career is built, fewer trips are taken. Once you have a family more trips are taken.
```{r ntrips, echo=TRUE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
par(mar=c(4,4,1,0.5))
data$log_ntrips <- log(data$ntrips+1)
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, "ntrips", x="age", g="nogroup", legend_placement="topleft")
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, "log_ntrips", x="age", g="nogroup", legend_placement="topleft")
```

However, on closer look (having the true clustering variable `g` at disposal) there could be seen 3 groups of different evolution.

Interpretation:

* group 1 (red): families earlier, but not many trips due to low income;
* group 2 (green): not many trips during studies, then high increase to enjoy, then less trips when starting a family, as the kids are older more trips;
* group 3 (blue): hard-workers, not many trips taken despite having high income, if some trip taken then probably long and expensive. 
```{r grouped_ntrips, echo=TRUE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
par(mar=c(4,4,1,0.5))
COL <- rainbow_hcl(3, c = 80, l = 50)
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, "ntrips", x="age", g="g", legend_placement="topleft", add_lowess=FALSE)
for(g in 1:3){
  subdata <- data[data$g == g,]
  lines(lowess(exp(subdata$pred_poi) ~ subdata$age, f = 1/3), col = COL[g], lwd = 3)
}
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, "log_ntrips", x="age", g="g", legend_placement="topleft", add_lowess=FALSE)
for(g in 1:3){
  subdata <- data[data$g == g,]
  lines(lowess(subdata$pred_poi ~ subdata$age, f = 1/3), col = COL[g], lwd = 3)
}
```

### Ordinal outcome - level of satisfaction vs. age
Men were also asked about their own (dis)satisfaction level: 0=dissatisfied < 1=neither-nor < 2=satisfied. 

Interpretation:

* group 1 (red): no clear evolution in time,
* group 2 (green): dissatisfied during studies but once finished they enjoy life (with high income),
* group 3 (blue): hard-workers who spent too much time working and not relaxing. 
```{r satisfaction, echo=TRUE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
tapply(data$satisfaction, data$g, summary)
par(mfrow = c(1,2), mar=c(4,4,1,0.5))
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, "satisfaction", x="age", g="nogroup")
plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(data, "satisfaction", x="age", g="g")
```

The question is whether we are able to discover these latent groups from the available data: `i`, `age`, `income`, `ntrips`, `satisfaction`. 

## Preparation for the estimation
```{r formula, echo=TRUE}
# splines
degree <- 2
knots <- c(18, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40)
inner <- knots[-c(1, length(knots))]
bound <- knots[c(1, length(knots))]
splB <- bs(data$age, knots = inner, Boundary.knots = bound, 
           degree = degree, intercept = FALSE)
spldim <- dim(splB)[2]
bsnames <- paste0("bs",1:spldim)
data[,bsnames] <- splB

# outcomes and regressors to be used
family <- c("num", "poi", "ord") # is also equivalent to
family <- c("gaussian", "poisson", "cumulative")
names(family) <- Ys <- c("income", "ntrips", "satisfaction")

id <- "i"
formula1 <- formula2 <- list()
for(y in Ys){
  # formula1 = group-specific linear trends
  formula1[[y]] <- list()
  formula1[[y]]$fixed <- as.formula("~ 1")
  formula1[[y]]$group <- as.formula("~ age")
  formula1[[y]]$random <- as.formula("~ 1")
  formula1[[y]]$offset <- ""
  
  # formula2 = group-specific spline curves
  formula2[[y]] <- list()
  formula2[[y]]$fixed <- as.formula("~ 1")
  formula2[[y]]$group <- as.formula(paste0("~ ", paste(bsnames, collapse = " + ")))
  formula2[[y]]$random <- as.formula("~ 1")
  formula2[[y]]$offset <- ""
}

# Group-specificity of other model parameters
(varying <- default_varying())
varying["prec_num"] <- FALSE
```

## Sampling MCMC chains for numerical outcome only
```{r mcmc0, message=FALSE, echo=TRUE, results=TRUE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
iter = 1000
set.seed(12345)
mcmc0 <- clustGLMM(formula = formula2, id = id, family = family["income"], data = data,
                   G = 3, varying = varying, iter = iter, nchains = 1, howsave = "matrix")

# preserve the interpretation of cluster labels by permuting cluster-specific parameters
perm <- list()
perm[[1]] <- c(2, 1, 3) 
mcmc0 <- permute_cluster_labels(mcmc0, perm)

mcmc0

plot(mcmc0)
plot(mcmc0, "beta_num", thin = 1, chains = 1)
plot(mcmc0, "beta_num", which="clusters_kerneldensity", thin = 1, chains = 1)
plot(mcmc0, "prec_num")
plot(mcmc0, "prec_num", burnin=100)
```

```{r clusteringU, echo=TRUE}
clusteringU <- function(mcmc, data, id, threshold = 0.5){
  clusteringU <- mcmc$clustering
  clusteringU[mcmc$certainty < threshold] <- 0
  
  # proposed clustering by each chain separately
  for(ch in 1:mcmc$nchains){
    data[, paste0("clustering", ch)] <- clusteringU[data[, id], ch]
    data[, paste0("certainty", ch)] <- mcmc$certainty[data[, id], ch]
  }
  
  return(data)
}
```

```{r clusteringU_mcmc0, echo=TRUE}
data <- clusteringU(mcmc0, data, id = id, threshold = 0.5)
data1 <- data[data$j==1, ]
# Confusion matrix for the first sampled chain
table(data1$clustering1, data1$g)
```

```{r codamcmc0, echo=TRUE}
# transform the outputs into coda format
codamcmc0 <- as_coda(mcmc0)
sumcodamcmc0 <- summary(codamcmc0)
# coda summaries
sumcodamcmc0$statistics[grep("beta_num", rownames(sumcodamcmc0$statistics)), ]
# or just use
summary(mcmc0)
print(summary(mcmc0), summary_type="quantiles")
```

```{r codamcmc0_income, echo=TRUE, results=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
par(mar=c(4,4,1,0.5))
age_grid <- seq(18, 40, by = 0.1)
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, "income", x="age", g="clustering1", legend_placement="topleft", add_lowess = FALSE)

newdata <- data.frame(age = age_grid)
newdata[, bsnames] <- bs(age_grid, knots = inner, Boundary.knots = bound, 
                         degree = degree, intercept = FALSE)
# samples method
predg <- predict(mcmc0, newdata, y="income", type="lp", what="fg", method="samples", gs=1:mcmc0$G, chain=1, burnin=100)
# plugin method
# predg <- predict(mcmc0, newdata, type="lp", what="fg", method="plugin", gs=1:mcmc0$G, chain=1, burnin=100)
for(g in 1:3){
  lines(x = age_grid,
        y = predg$fit[,paste0("(",g,")")],
        col = COL[g], lwd = 3)
  if(!is.null(predg$lwr)){
    lines(x = age_grid,
          y = predg$lwr[,paste0("(",g,")")],
          col = COL[g], lty = 2)
  }
  if(!is.null(predg$upr)){
    lines(x = age_grid,
          y = predg$upr[,paste0("(",g,")")],
          col = COL[g], lty = 2)
  }
}
```

## Sampling MCMC chains for linear trends of all three outcome
```{r mcmc1, message=FALSE, echo=TRUE, results=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
set.seed(12345)
mcmc1 <- clustGLMM(formula = formula1, id = id, family = family, data = data,
                   G = 3, varying = varying, iter = iter, nchains = 1)
# preserve the interpretation of cluster labels by permuting cluster-specific parameters
perm <- list()
perm[[1]] <- c(2, 1, 3) 
mcmc1 <- permute_cluster_labels(mcmc1, perm)

mcmc1

plot(mcmc1)

plot(mcmc1, "beta_num", thin = 1, chains = 1)
plot(mcmc1, "beta_num", which="clusters_kerneldensity")
plot(mcmc1, "prec_num", which="clusters_kerneldensity")

plot(mcmc1, "beta_poi", thin = 1, chains = 1)
plot(mcmc1, "beta_poi", which="clusters_kerneldensity")

plot(mcmc1, "beta_ord", thin = 1, chains = 1)
plot(mcmc1, "beta_ord", which="clusters_kerneldensity")
plot(mcmc1, "c_ord", which="clusters_kerneldensity")
```

```{r clusteringU_mcmc1, echo=TRUE}
data <- clusteringU(mcmc1, data, id = id, threshold = 0.5)
data1 <- data[data$j==1, ]
# Confusion matrix for the first sampled chain
table(data1$clustering1, data1$g)
```

```{r codamcmc1, echo=TRUE}
# transform the outputs into coda format
codamcmc1 <- as_coda(mcmc1)

# coda summaries
sumcodamcmc1$statistics[grep("beta_num", rownames(sumcodamcmc1$statistics)), ]

sumcodamcmc1$statistics[grep("beta_ord", rownames(sumcodamcmc1$statistics)), ]
sumcodamcmc1$statistics[grep("c_ord", rownames(sumcodamcmc1$statistics)), ]
# or just use
```



## Sampling MCMC chains for spline trends for all three outcomes
```{r mcmc2, message=FALSE, echo=TRUE, results=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
set.seed(12345)
mcmc2 <- clustGLMM(formula = formula2, id = id, family = family, data = data,
                   G = 3, varying = varying, iter = iter, nchains = 1)
# preserve the interpretation of cluster labels by permuting cluster-specific parameters
perm <- list()
perm[[1]] <- c(2, 3, 1) 
mcmc2 <- permute_cluster_labels(mcmc2, perm)

mcmc2

plot(mcmc2, "ng")

plot(mcmc2, "beta_num", thin = 1, chains = 1)
plot(mcmc2, "beta_num", which="clusters_kerneldensity")
plot(mcmc2, "prec_num", which="clusters_kerneldensity")

plot(mcmc2, "beta_poi", thin = 1, chains = 1)
plot(mcmc2, "beta_poi", which="clusters_kerneldensity")

plot(mcmc2, "beta_ord", thin = 1, chains = 1)
plot(mcmc2, "beta_ord", which="clusters_kerneldensity")
plot(mcmc2, "c_ord", which="clusters_kerneldensity")
```

```{r clusteringU_mcmc2, echo=TRUE}
data <- clusteringU(mcmc2, data, id = id, threshold = 0.5)
data1 <- data[data$j==1, ]
# Confusion matrix for the first sampled chain
table(data1$clustering1, data1$g)
```

```{r codamcmc2, echo=TRUE}
# transform the outputs into coda format
codamcmc2 <- as_coda(mcmc2)
sumcodamcmc2 <- summary(codamcmc2)
# coda summaries
sumcodamcmc2$statistics[grep("beta_num", rownames(sumcodamcmc2$statistics)), ]
sumcodamcmc2$quantiles[grep("beta_num", rownames(sumcodamcmc2$quantiles)), ]
sumcodamcmc2$statistics[grep("beta_poi", rownames(sumcodamcmc2$statistics)), ]
sumcodamcmc2$statistics[grep("beta_ord", rownames(sumcodamcmc2$statistics)), ]
sumcodamcmc2$statistics[grep("c_ord", rownames(sumcodamcmc2$statistics)), ]
```

```{r codamcmc2_income, echo=TRUE, results=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
par(mar=c(4,4,1,0.5))
age_grid <- seq(18, 40, by = 0.1)
plot_num_vs_x_grouped(data, "income", x="age", g="clustering1", legend_placement="topleft", add_lowess = FALSE)
for(g in 1:3){
  rows <- grep(paste0("beta_num_income\\(",g,"\\)"), rownames(sumcodamcmc2$statistics))
  beta_num <- sumcodamcmc2$statistics[rows, "Mean"]
  lines(x = age_grid,
        y = beta_num[1] + bs(age_grid, knots = inner, Boundary.knots = bound, 
                             degree = degree, intercept = FALSE) %*% as.matrix(beta_num[-1]),
        col = COL[g], lwd = 3)
}
```

```{r codamcmc2_satisfaction, echo=TRUE, results=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
par(mar=c(4,4,1,0.5))
plot(0, 0, type="n", xlim = range(data$age), ylim = c(-4, 4), xlab = "age", ylab = "satisfaction")
for(g in 1:3){
  rows <- grep(paste0("beta_ord_satisfaction\\(",g,"\\)"), rownames(sumcodamcmc2$statistics))
  beta_ord <- sumcodamcmc2$statistics[rows, "Mean"]
  rows <- grep(paste0("c_ord_satisfaction\\(",g,"\\)"), rownames(sumcodamcmc2$statistics))
  c_ord <- sumcodamcmc2$statistics[rows, "Mean"]
  for(l in 1:2){
    lines(x = age_grid,
          y = -c_ord[l] + bs(age_grid, knots = inner, Boundary.knots = bound,
                             degree = degree, intercept = FALSE) %*% as.matrix(beta_ord),
          col = COL[g], lwd = 3)
  }
}
```
